actions.user_requirement: The tab-bar nav links were still rendering WP-admin's default blue, not the intended white (user pasted the rendered HTML + WP core's own body/a CSS as evidence). actions.action: Root-caused the color bug: Tailwind v4 puts every utility inside a CSS @layer, and WP core's own admin CSS is unlayered — per the cascade-layers spec, unlayered rules always beat layered ones regardless of selector specificity, so WP core's plain 'a { color: #3858e9 }' overrode '.text-white' even though a class selector normally beats an element selector. Fixed by applying Tailwind v4's trailing '!' important-modifier (border-white!, text-white!, text-white/70!, hover:text-white!) to the four color utilities in the nav, and verified '!important' actually landed in the compiled CSS before considering it fixed. Documented as knoladge/tailwind-cascade-layers-vs-wp-admin.md (noted this likely affects other admin links too, not fixed elsewhere since only the nav was reported). Built the child-theme feature: inc/child-theme.php (loaded unconditionally, mirroring inc/updater.php's pattern) with hex_generate_child_theme_slug() (collision-avoiding), hex_child_theme_style_css()/hex_child_theme_functions_php() (pure content builders, with a hex_strip_comment_terminator() defense against a theme name breaking out of the style.css header comment), hex_create_child_theme() (writes via WP_Filesystem — deliberately not unit-tested, matching the 'don't test the actual filesystem/API edge' policy already set for the main updater), and a fully separate PucFactory-based update checker for the child theme (own hex_child_github_repo/branch/activation_key options, own settings group, targets wp_get_theme($slug)'s own style.css so it works whether or not the child is the active theme). Design decision: all management (create/check/update) lives in the parent theme's admin rather than generating a duplicate mini-admin-UI into the child, since WordPress always loads the parent's functions.php even when the child is active. Added a 4th admin page/tab 'Child Theme' (inc/admin/page-child-theme.php) with a create form, a separate settings form, and Check/Update buttons; 3 new admin-post handlers; child settings fields in inc/admin/settings.php reusing hex_sanitize_github_branch() and a near-duplicate hex_sanitize_child_github_repo() (separate settings-error identifier). Added tests/ChildThemeTest.php (11 new tests) — full suite 47 tests/63 assertions passing. Fixed 2 WPCS docblock full-stop errors (hash-notation @param blocks weren't accepted by this ruleset — switched to plain single-line @param descriptions) and auto-fixed alignment warnings; 0 phpcs errors. Per the new version-bump rule, bumped 1.0.1 -> 1.0.2 in all three places. Wrote features/child-theme.md and knoladge/tailwind-cascade-layers-vs-wp-admin.md; updated project.json/claude.md.

Instead the child's functions.php enqueues only its own stylesheet, with an explicit dependency on the parent's registered 'hex-tailwind' handle for correct load order. actions.user_requirement: The child theme (hexnity-wp-child, the hand-written starter theme created earlier) is actually active on the site, but the Child Theme admin page still shows 'Install Child Theme' instead of an activated status — a real bug report.
actions.action: Root-caused: hex_is_child_theme_active()/hex_get_child_theme_slug() relied entirely on the hex_child_theme_slug OPTION, which is only ever written by hex_install_child_theme_from_repo(). The user had activated hexnity-wp-child by copying/activating it directly (not through the Fetch & Install button), so that option was never set, and the code had no way to know a child theme was active regardless of reality. Fixed by making hex_get_child_theme_slug() prefer WordPress's own live state: `is_child_theme() ? get_stylesheet() : get_option('hex_child_theme_slug','')` — the insight being that this code only executes because it's required from THIS theme's own functions.php, and WordPress always loads the parent's functions.php even when a child is active, so is_child_theme() being true here proves the active child's parent IS this theme, regardless of how that child reached disk or got activated. hex_is_child_theme_active() simplified to just is_child_theme() directly. This single change also fixes hex_check_for_child_theme_update()/hex_perform_child_theme_update(), which had the identical blind spot. Rewrote the affected tests in tests/ChildThemeTest.php (is_child_theme()-based mocking instead of get_option-based) and added 2 new ones for hex_get_child_theme_slug()'s live-vs-stored preference — full suite 53 tests/60 assertions passing, 0 phpcs errors, php -l clean. Bumped 1.0.4 -> 1.0.5 in all three version locations. Wrote knoladge/child-theme-active-detection-bug.md (the failure, root cause, fix, and the general takeaway: prefer the platform's own source of truth over a private tracking flag when both represent the same fact) and updated features/child-theme.md and project.json accordingly.

actions.user_requirement: Develop a full theme style setup: H1-H6 + additional text-size variations, spacing variations, colors, button paddings/radius (like YOOtheme Pro) — with an admin 'Theme Options' menu. Editing should require an active child theme (disabled + a message asking for one, otherwise). Cover almost all style settings available in YOOtheme Pro, clearly documented for future AI use. Changing a value in the admin (e.g. font size) must change the front end everywhere, live.
actions.action: Built a ~27-token admin-configurable design-token system. Architecture: a single PHP schema (hex_get_style_schema() in the new inc/style-settings.php, loaded unconditionally) drives everything — Settings API registration (hex_register_style_settings() in inc/admin/settings.php, one generic hex_render_style_field() renderer for all fields instead of ~27 hand-written ones), sanitization (hex_sanitize_style_length()/hex_sanitize_style_color(), both reject-and-revert-to-previous-value rather than ever storing empty/invalid — uses current_filter() to recover the option name inside the generic sanitize_option_{name} filter context), and the runtime CSS output (hex_render_style_css_vars(), hooked to wp_head, prints every current value as a --hex-{key} custom property on :root on EVERY front-end request, independent of child-theme-active state — plus hex_is_safe_style_value() as an independent output-time injection defense on top of the sanitize callbacks). Groups: typography (h1-h6 + body/lead/large/small — 10), spacing (xs/sm/md/lg/xl/2xl — 6), colors (primary/secondary/accent/muted/text/background — 6), buttons (radius + default/small/large padding-x/y — 7), radius (card — 1). Live-without-rebuild mechanism: new assets/css/src/site-theme.css defines Tailwind v4 @theme tokens as `var(--hex-{key}, {default})` — e.g. `--text-h1: var(--hex-h1-size, 2.5rem)` — so Tailwind's compiled .text-h1 utility references the runtime variable, not a baked-in value; verified this actual chain in the compiled CSS output, not just assumed it. All token names deliberately avoid colliding with Tailwind's own built-in scale (h1-h6/body/lead/large/small instead of xs/sm/lg/xl; site-primary/etc instead of blue/slate; button/card instead of sm/md/lg) so this never silently overrides existing Tailwind usage elsewhere. Also added a .btn component (+ -secondary/-accent/-outline/-sm/-lg variants), a global `a { color: var(--color-site-primary) }` base-layer default link color (loses to any more-specific existing utility via ordinary specificity), and .prose h1-h6 overrides (@tailwindcss/typography's own documented override pattern) so headings an editor types inside post content also respond to the H1-H6 settings, not just template-level titles. Gating: inc/admin/page-theme-options.php wraps every field in `<fieldset disabled>` unless hex_is_child_theme_active(), with an amber notice + link to the Child Theme page when disabled — reusing the active-detection fixed in the previous entry. Added the 5th admin tab/submenu (menu.php, partials.php) and a Dashboard quick link. Retrofitted existing front-end templates to actually use the new tokens (so the feature has real, visible effect today, not just for future pages): archive.php/404.php/search.php (h1 titles -> text-h1), comments.php (title -> text-h3, closed-notice -> text-small), template-parts/content-none.php (title -> text-h2, card -> rounded-card/p-lg), template-parts/content.php (h1/h2 titles -> text-h1/text-h2, link hover -> hover:text-site-primary, card -> rounded-card/p-md, meta/footer -> text-small), template-parts/content-page.php (title -> text-h1, page-links -> text-small), footer.php (site-info -> text-small), header.php (site-title fallback -> text-large) — chose exact-default-matching values (p-md=1.5rem=old p-6, p-lg=2rem=old p-8) where possible so today's visual output doesn't change, only becomes admin-controllable. Added tests/StyleSettingsTest.php (17 tests: schema shape, naming transforms, value resolution, CSS-var output incl. the unsafe-value-skip defense, both sanitize callbacks' revert-on-invalid behavior) — full suite 69 tests/100 assertions passing, 0 phpcs errors (after auto-fixing 23 array-alignment warnings and fixing 2 more hash-notation-docblock full-stop errors, the same WPCS friction point hit twice before), php -l clean, both CSS builds compile with all new utility classes verified present via grep. Wrote features/design-system.md — the explicit 'for future AI use' reference this was asked for, including a full class-substitution table (design-system class vs. the raw Tailwind equivalent to avoid) and a step-by-step 'adding a new token' guide. Added a MANDATORY claude.md rule pointing every future front-end styling task at that table. Bumped 1.0.5 -> 1.1.0 (minor, new feature) in all three version locations.

actions.user_requirement: The first design-token system (27 fields) was 'not completed' — user wants massive YOOtheme-Pro-scale coverage (100+ settings), basics like line-height/letter-spacing were missing, and the settings UI (a flat WP form-table) was 'not good' / needed something 'more professional'.
actions.action: Rebuilt the schema from 27 to 146 fields across 12 groups (was 5): Typography (heading levels now carry size+line-height+letter-spacing+weight+margin-bottom each, plus body/lead/large/small/meta with their own line-heights, plus body/heading font-family and link color/hover-color = 47 fields, up from 10), Spacing (unchanged, 6), Colors (expanded from 6 to a 15-color palette: primary/secondary/tertiary/accent/success/warning/danger/info/muted/emphasis/body-bg/body-text/inverse-bg/inverse-text/border), Buttons (expanded from 7 to 26: 4 full variants — default/primary/secondary/danger, each background+color+hover pair — plus text-button colors, radius, weight, 6 paddings), and 6 entirely new groups: Forms (8), Cards (6), Sections (8), Global radius (3, deliberately overrides Tailwind's own rounded-sm/md/lg site-wide), Tables (4), Alerts (8, 4 states), Badges (10, 5 variants), Icons (5). Introduced 4 new field types beyond length/color: 'number' (bare unitless line-heights), 'weight' (100-900 enum), 'shadow' (fixed keyword->real-box-shadow-CSS preset map, since raw box-shadow syntax can't safely round-trip through a text field), 'font' (safe font-family charset). Refactored sanitization: every type-specific sanitizer now shares one hex_style_revert_from_filter() helper (previously length/color had near-duplicate revert logic). Built the schema with per-family loops (heading levels, button/alert/badge variants) rather than hand-writing 146 array literals — one config change adds a whole family member. Rebuilt the admin UI per the 'not professional' complaint: replaced the flat form-table (do_settings_section/do_settings_fields) with a left-category tab nav + right detail panel (inc/admin/page-theme-options.php + new assets/js/admin.js tab-switching logic), a CSS-grid 2-column field layout instead of table rows, and native <input type=color> swatches paired with (and JS-synced to) the hex text fields instead of plain text-only color inputs. Rewrote site-theme.css to wire every new token: added @layer base rules applying full typographic treatment directly to bare h1-h6/body/a tags (so ANY heading anywhere gets the treatment, not just ones with an explicit text-h* class) and removed now-redundant/conflicting font-bold/font-semibold/tracking-tight utility classes from every retrofitted heading (they were higher-specificity than the new base rules and would have silently overridden them); added .card/.form-control+.form-label/.table-styled/.alert+4 variants/.badge+5 variants/.icon components; expanded .btn to 4 real variants (default/primary/secondary/danger) plus .btn-text/.btn-outline; extended the .prose heading overrides to include line-height/letter-spacing/weight, not just font-size. Swapped the 3 existing card usages (template-parts/content.php, content-none.php, 404.php) from ad-hoc utility composition to the real .card component. Verified in compiled CSS: .card, base h1{}, body{}, and the --radius-sm/md/lg override of rounded-sm/md/lg all resolved correctly. Needed to insert 25 individual '/* translators: %s: ... */' comments (one per sprintf(__(...)) call site in the loop-built schema, each describing the specific interpolated variable) to satisfy WPCS's WordPress.WP.I18n.MissingTranslatorsComment sniff — did this with a small Python script matching each sprintf pattern rather than by hand, then verified zero unmatched patterns. Rewrote tests/StyleSettingsTest.php's group-coverage test to check schema membership against hex_get_style_groups() dynamically (was a hardcoded 5-group list that would need updating every time a group is added) and added tests for all 4 new field types plus shadow-keyword CSS resolution — suite grew from 69 to 85 tests (100 to 419 assertions, since several new tests loop-assert or check large arrays). Rewrote features/design-system.md and the claude.md pointer rule around the full new class/component set. Bumped 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0 in all three version locations.

actions.action: Root cause: the previous round's ! important-modifier fix (needed because WP-admin core CSS is unlayered and beats layered Tailwind utilities) was only applied to the new isolated components (.hex-field, .hex-btn-*, .notice, .form-table, sidebar nav links) — every plain heading/paragraph/badge/link scattered through the five page bodies still used un-!'d text-color utilities (text-white, text-gray-400, text-indigo-400, etc.), which were losing to WP core's own default text color on the new dark backgrounds. Fixed via a one-off Python regex script run across inc/admin/partials.php and all 5 page files, converting every remaining bare text-color utility (text-white/black/gray-NNN/indigo-NNN/emerald-NNN/amber-NNN/red-NNN/hexnity-NNN, with or without an opacity modifier or hover:/variant prefix) to its !-suffixed form wherever not already present — 67 replacements. Also hand-updated assets/js/admin.js's classList.toggle() calls (text-white -> text-white!, text-gray-400 -> text-gray-400!) since those live in a JS file, not scanned PHP markup. Separately, bumped the sidebar logo from h-7 to h-11 (and its container padding py-5 to py-6) in hex_render_admin_shell_start() per 'make the logo little bigger'. Documented as a 'Follow-up bug' section appended to knoladge/admin-dark-theme-components.md, with an explicit lesson: treat ! as the default for text-color utilities inside .hex-admin, not an exception applied only where a bug was previously spotted.

actions.user_requirement: User pasted the Theme Options page's category tab button markup and, after clarifying, said: "now bg is white, I need dark bg, without any borders. color should be white."
actions.action: Root cause: assets/css/src/admin.css deliberately skips Tailwind's Preflight reset (documented in its own file header) so it doesn't clobber the rest of wp-admin's chrome. That means a bare <button> element (the Theme Options page's .hex-tab-btn category tabs, inc/admin/page-theme-options.php) keeps the browser's native white/bordered widget appearance -- nothing had ever reset it. User confirmed: resting tabs showed a white background with a visible border and gray text, instead of fitting the dark dashboard. Fix: added a .hex-tab-btn component rule in assets/css/src/admin.css (@layer components): `cursor-pointer appearance-none border-none! text-white!` -- appearance-none + border-none! strip the native chrome (background falls back to the CSS-initial transparent, letting the dark nav's own bg-gray-900 show through), text-white! makes the label readable. Deliberately did NOT set a background-color in the component: this file's `@layer components` block is declared after `@layer utilities` in the source, so per CSS cascade-layer rules a normal-importance background rule in .hex-tab-btn would have beaten the page's own `hover:bg-gray-800` utility (a different, earlier-declared layer) regardless of specificity or hover state -- leaving the hover highlight permanently unreachable. Leaving background alone avoids that layer fight entirely. Simplified the inline classes on the button (inc/admin/page-theme-options.php) by dropping the now-redundant/conflicting text-gray-400!/hover:text-gray-200! utilities, since color is now owned by the component. Also simplified assets/js/admin.js's tab-activation handler: it used to toggle text-gray-400!/text-white! per tab on click; since every tab is white at rest now (differentiated only by the active tab's bg-indigo-600), removed the now-dead text-color toggling and kept only the background toggle. Rebuilt CSS (npm run build:css) and verified the compiled output. Bumped version 1.5.1 -> 1.5.2 in style.css, functions.php, tests/bootstrap.php. Ran vendor/bin/phpunit (103/103) and vendor/bin/phpcs --standard=phpcs.xml.dist (0 errors/warnings).

actions.user_requirement: User, frustrated that the previous fix (1.5.2) still showed a white background on the tab buttons, said the CSS should be `.hex-tab-btn { ...; background-color: black; }` and asked for it to be added like that.
actions.action: Previous fix (1.5.2) deliberately left .hex-tab-btn without any background-color, reasoning that appearance-none would make the background fall back to CSS-initial transparent. That reasoning was wrong: the browser's UA stylesheet sets an *explicit* background-color (ButtonFace/white) on <button>, independent of the appearance property -- appearance:none stops the native widget from being drawn, it does not clear that explicit UA background declaration. With no author rule overriding it, the button stayed white, which is what the user was still seeing ("fuck why cannt u still add dark color to that buttons. still they are white"). User then specified the exact fix wanted: add `background-color: black;` directly to .hex-tab-btn. Implemented via `bg-black!` in the component's @apply list. Because .hex-tab-btn's @layer components block is declared after admin.css's `@layer utilities` import, a plain (non-important) black background would have permanently beaten the page's hover:bg-gray-800 utility and the JS-toggled active bg-indigo-600 utility (cascade layers decide ties for equal-importance rules by declaration order, ignoring specificity) -- so both hover and active-tab highlighting would have gone dark/invisible. Fixed by making all three competing declarations !important, which moves the comparison to the importance tier instead (where the *earlier* declared layer wins, i.e. utilities beats components): changed the page's `hover:bg-gray-800` to `hover:bg-gray-800!` (inc/admin/page-theme-options.php) and admin.js's toggled class from `bg-indigo-600` to `bg-indigo-600!` (assets/js/admin.js). Verified in the compiled CSS that all three rules (.hex-tab-btn's bg-black!important, hover:bg-gray-800!:hover !important, .bg-indigo-600\!:not(:hover) !important) came out correctly. Rebuilt CSS. Bumped version 1.5.2 -> 1.5.3 in style.css, functions.php, tests/bootstrap.php. Ran vendor/bin/phpunit (103/103) and vendor/bin/phpcs --standard=phpcs.xml.dist (0 errors/warnings).

actions.user_requirement: User pasted the Google Fonts field UI and reported pasting an embed URL didn't make it show up below; asked: "here u have to add repeater, if I add font it should visible in font selector as drop down."

The remove button needed the same !important-vs-layer-order treatment documented in knoladge/admin-bare-button-reset-and-layer-order.md (px-3! to shrink .hex-btn's own later-declared-layer padding). Documented the no-JS caveat (unnamed row inputs mean editing requires JS, consistent with the rest of this dashboard) in knoladge/google-fonts-picker.md. Rebuilt CSS, verified new utility classes (px-3!, space-y-2, hidden) compiled correctly. Bumped version 1.5.3 -> 1.5.4 in style.css, functions.php, tests/bootstrap.php. actions.action:
User asked how Theme Options worked, then explicitly requested it be rearchitected: 'no db option doesnt work. it should be css file and while developing child theme if any value doesnt belong to these availabel stuffs, then should create new css class and then it should show in this options panel. develop full architecture how these should create and how it automatically detect this admin page and show. then document it then next time while child theme development it should follow.' Used EnterPlanMode: one Explore agent surveyed the current DB-based implementation (inc/style-settings.php's ~146-field schema/Settings-API flow, site-theme.css's var(--hex-key,default) fallback pattern, StyleSettingsTest.php's get_option mocking, inc/child-theme.php's Theme_Upgrader-only file-write precedent), then one Plan agent validated and refined a proposed architecture (corrected the custom-type sanitize regex, the type-guessing order, forced the Google Fonts save into the same handler since it shares one <form>, and identified the hard WP_Mock constraint that project-defined functions/native filesystem calls can't be mocked in this test suite, which drove which new functions had to be pure vs. thin-and-untested). Plan approved, then implemented: 

inc/style-settings.php: values now live in {active child theme}/theme-options.css, not wp_options. Added hex_style_tokens_file_path(), hex_parse_style_tokens_css() (pure regex parser), hex_get_child_theme_tokens() (reads+parses the file; deliberately NOT static-cached -- a static cache would leak across PHPUnit tests since the whole suite runs in one PHP process, discovered and fixed before writing tests), hex_guess_style_type() (color/length/number/font/custom, never weight/shadow -- those are closed enumerations a wrong guess could mangle), hex_merge_style_schema_with_tokens() (adds a 'custom'-group entry for every file token not already in hex_get_style_schema()), hex_get_effective_style_schema()/_groups()/_values() (the merged view everything admin-facing now uses), hex_build_style_tokens_css() (ports the old hex_render_style_css_vars()'s safety re-check + shadow resolution into a pure file-content builder), hex_enqueue_child_theme_tokens() (wp_enqueue_scripts; enqueues the file directly, filemtime()-versioned, in place of the old inline <style id=hex-style-vars> block -- safer since it's parsed as a real stylesheet resource, never inlined into HTML). Renamed hex_style_option_name() -> hex_style_field_name() (no longer a literal option name, still needed for form field name/id). Refactored all 6 existing hex_sanitize_style_*() to be pure (return null on failure instead of add_settings_error()+hex_style_revert_from_filter()'s current_filter()-sniffing trick, which only worked inside the Settings API pipeline); added hex_sanitize_style_custom() (narrow allowlist, no ':' at all, explicit url() reject, 200-char cap) for the new auto-detected 'custom' type; added hex_sanitize_submitted_style_tokens() (pure: sanitizes a full submission against a schema, reports rejected field labels). Deleted hex_render_style_css_vars()/its wp_head hook, hex_style_revert_from_filter(), hex_style_key_from_option_name(). 

inc/admin/settings.php: deleted hex_register_style_settings() entirely (no more register_setting() for the 146 fields or for hex_google_fonts_urls); hex_render_style_field()/hex_render_style_group_fields() now use hex_style_field_name()/hex_get_effective_style_schema(); added a 'custom' field-type case and hex_style_field_placeholder_for_type(). 

inc/admin/handlers.php: added hex_handle_save_style_options() (admin_post_hex_save_style_options) -- capability+nonce check, HARD server-side hex_is_child_theme_active() check (closes a real gap: previously only an HTML disabled attribute prevented saving with no active child theme), sanitizes tokens + the Google Fonts field (still DB-backed, folded in here since its repeater shares this page's one <form>), writes theme-options.css via WP_Filesystem, transient-based result message. 

inc/admin/page-theme-options.php: form now posts to admin-post.php instead of options.php; dropped settings_fields()/settings_errors() for a wp_nonce_field()+transient-log pattern matching every other admin page in this dashboard; switched to the effective schema/groups so a 'Custom Tokens' tab can appear. inc/admin/page-dashboard.php: its stat tile now counts hex_get_effective_style_schema(). 

assets/css/src/site-theme.css: updated the header comment describing the new file-based mechanism (no functional change, comment-only, but rebuilt CSS anyway for consistency). 

tests/StyleSettingsTest.php: rewritten (49 tests, up from 32) -- deleted the option-name-strip test and the 3 render tests (assertions ported onto hex_build_style_tokens_css(), now pure/no mocking); rewrote the 6 sanitize-reject tests to assert null; rewrote the two storage-touching tests to mock is_child_theme()->false (the only WP-core call in the new read path, since project-defined functions and native file I/O can't be mocked in this suite -- documented as a real constraint, not a gap); added tests for the parser, type-guesser, schema-merger, CSS-builder (incl. the new custom type), and the submitted-tokens sanitizer. 

Documentation (the explicit point of the request): new knoladge/child-theme-css-token-architecture.md (full architecture, the 'adding a new token' workflow for future child-theme development, the testing-constraint rationale, why no static caching); updated features/design-system.md (storage section, field-type table, adding-a-token workflow split into parent-schema vs. child-theme-custom paths, files/tests sections, a new known-gap about the untested live file-write path), features/child-theme.md (cross-reference), CLAUDE.md's Known project state paragraph and test count. Bumped version 1.5.4 -> 1.5.5 in style.css, functions.php, tests/bootstrap.php. Updated project.json's per-file entries for every touched inc/ and tests/ file. actions.user_requirement: User pasted a fluid-typography CSS reference (a clamp()-based font-size scale with mobile/desktop breakpoints, plus @font-face declarations) from a different site of theirs, said "I asked to implement this" -- after I flagged that nothing in that pasted code (resko/ppm-child paths, UIKit classes, WooCommerce selectors, Bizmo font) matched this repo and asked whether it belonged here, user clarified: "no this is my code, so I want u to implement this clamp logic for fluid typo. check how they implemented and implement this. but makesure to rename all according to this project. also update theme options also."
actions.action: Found the actual clamp()-based fluid-typography mechanism (hex_get_fluid_size_pairs(), hex_build_fluid_clamp(), the {level}_size_mobile/_desktop schema pairs for every heading level H1-H6 and body-level text style body/lead/large/small/meta, two new 'global'-group breakpoint fields fluid_mobile_breakpoint/fluid_desktop_breakpoint, and hex_build_style_tokens_css()'s derived-clamp-declaration logic) already present and fully working in inc/style-settings.php's uncommitted working tree, with matching tests already in tests/StyleSettingsTest.php (127/127 passing) and phpcs clean (0 errors/warnings) -- the code itself was already a correct, project-renamed (hex_*/--hex-* only, no 'resko' reference anywhere) port of the technique, and the admin field renderer (inc/admin/settings.php) and Theme Options page (inc/admin/page-theme-options.php) already handled the new mobile/desktop field pairs generically with no changes needed. What was actually still pending, per this project's own update rules, was the documentation/version-bump half of the work: updated project.json's inc/style-settings.php and tests/StyleSettingsTest.php entries to describe the fluid pairs and their functions; added a new features/design-system.md 'Fluid typography' subsection (explaining the mobile/desktop-pair + shared-breakpoint model, that every other heading property stays a single static value, and where the derived --hex-{key}-size var is consumed) plus an 'Adding a new token' entry for adding a new fluid-sized field; wrote knoladge/fluid-typography-clamp.md documenting the source (the user's own different site, technique only -- no verbatim copying), the interpolation formula, why this project's schema stores real CSS lengths (rem/px) rather than the source's unitless-px-multiplied-by-1px trick, why the runtime division inside calc() needs CSS Values & Units Level 4 length/length-division support (works in all evergreen engines), and the derived-vs-stored key distinction that keeps a stale flat value from ever shadowing the computed clamp(). Updated claude.md's 'Known project state' (fluid-typography bullet, test count 120->127, version). Bumped version 1.5.5 -> 1.5.6 in style.css, functions.php, tests/bootstrap.php. Re-ran vendor/bin/phpunit (127/127) and vendor/bin/phpcs --standard=phpcs.xml.dist (0 errors/warnings) after the doc/version edits to confirm nothing broke.
